To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lysophosphatidylic acid (LPA), a lipid mediator that is increased during oxidant stress, induces endothelial cell cytotoxicity via the LPA(1)-receptor and by increasing inducible nitrite oxide synthase (iNOS) via p38 and JNK.

lysophosphatide acid (LPA)-induced cell death in endothelial cells involves LPA(1)-mediated activation of p38 MAPK and JNK, which leads to inducible nitrite oxide synthase expression and nitrosylation of cellular proteins, and the resultant oxidant stress causes cell death.
LPA causes endothelial death via an LPA(1)-receptor-dependent mechanism that involves the induction of iNOS and the generation of nitro-oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of LPA in the development of microvascular rarefaction in the ischemic brain.
a novel role of LPA in the pathogenesis of hypoxic-ischemia-induced brain injury.
the role of oxidant stress in the pathophysiology of ischemic injury to the neuromicrovasculature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LPA, by modulating the cell redox status, induces endothelial cell cytotoxicity via p38 MAPK, JNK, and NOS, which leads to neuromicrocirculatory rarefaction.
LPA is a novel mediator of oxidant stress-induced endothelial cell injury and that the redox environment plays a significant role therein.
LPA induces endothelial cell rarefaction by inducing NOS expression and nitrosylation of proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LPA, by virtue of its ability to modulate the redox environment of the cell, is capable of inducing endothelial cell death.
LPA is an endothelial cell cytotoxic mediator that is implicated in hypoxia-ischemia-induced neuromicrovascular damage.
LPA, by virtue of its ability to induce NOS expression and activity, causes a redox imbalance, which in turn induces endothelial cell cytotoxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LPA-induced oxidant stress is an important mechanism of hypoxic-ischemia-induced endothelial death and neuromicrovascular injury.
the LPA(1)-mediated endothelial cytotoxicity is a redox-dependent phenomenon.
LPA, a lipid mediator of oxidant stress, is a mediator of endothelial cell death.
